title: Autonomous Fallback Decision Engine for Region/Tier Routing
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a decision engine that automatically triggers safe, predictable fallbacks when region or tier routes exceed configured failure/overload signals (429 spikes, request timeouts, error-rate regressions). The engine should be pluggable into the smart routing layer and support model-variant fallbacks (e.g., quantized variant, lower-tier capacity) with cooldown, hysteresis, and priority-aware routing.

Key requirements:
- Ingest signals: per-route 429 rate, p95/p99 latency spikes, downstream model error-rate, GPU OOMs, region capacity signals, and token-level throttles.
- Composite trigger score: compute a weighted score combining short-term spike and sustained degradation. Allow dynamic weight overrides per-customer/tier.
- Actions supported: soft-degrade (reduce concurrency for route), model-variant fallback (switch to lower-cost compatible variant), region failover (primary->secondary region), tier fallback (dedicated->shared with quota throttle), and hard circuit-breaker (reject or queue).
- Safety: require multiple orthogonal signals or sustained window before hard cutover. Apply exponential backoff + randomized jitter for re-enable attempts.
- Observability: surface decision rationale in Console (event + signal snapshot), annotate traces, and publish metrics for decisions, durations, and rollback counts.
- Rollout: canary enable per-namespace; initial default thresholds conservative to avoid false positives.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive vs conservative triggers: aggressive reduces client errors quickly but increases risk of unnecessary degradation; we adopt two-tier thresholds (soft and hard) with separate SLOs and TTLs.
- Local (node) vs centralized decision: local decisions lower latency but harder to correlate cross-region; plan hybrid: local fast-path for short windows, centralized adjudicator for cross-region escalation.
- Model-variant compatibility: restrict automated fallback to compatible model family to avoid semantic regressions; require opt-in per customer for cross-model-family fallbacks.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Reduce user-facing 5xx+429 errors by >=40% in incidents where fallback triggers are applicable.
- False-positive fallback rate <=2% of triggered events in first 90 days.
- Mean time to recover (automatic roll-back) under 5 minutes for transient overloads.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests for score computation and hysteresis logic.
- Chaos tests that inject 429/timeouts at different magnitudes and validate chosen action.
- Staging canary against synthetic traffic and a subset of production namespaces (~1% traffic) with metrics dashboards and rollback alarms.
- Postmortem template to capture decision traces for any automatic fallback that causes customer impact.
tasks: Spec: finalize scoring formula and parameter set (weight defaults, window sizes)
Implement telemetry ingestion hooks for 429/latency/error signals
Build decision engine core (scoring, state machine, cooldown/hysteresis)
Integrate with routing plane: action API for model-variant switch / region failover / throttle
Console: decision event UI + link to trace and metric snapshot
E2E tests: chaos-engine scenarios + canary runbook
Run security review and add KMS/ACL checks for private deployments
acceptance_criteria: Decision engine evaluates composite score within 50ms of signal ingestion for local fast-path
Soft-degrade action reduces downstream p99 by >=20% in synthetic overload tests
Model-variant fallback respects customer opt-in flags and only selects compatible variants
All decision events are logged and visible in Console with raw signal snapshot
Automated rollback triggers if error-rate increases post-fallback above configured threshold
